title: Event handler deduplication uses unstable ids for weak bound methods
reasoning: Bound method handlers are stored via WeakMethod, and each access to wrapper.handler can materialize a fresh bound-method object. _dedupe_handlers then records id(handler), which is only stable for that transient object, not for the underlying instance/function pair. During MRO handler resolution this can fail to deduplicate the same subscribed method consistently, and object-id reuse can also incorrectly collapse distinct bound handlers. The result is incorrect publish behavior: duplicate handler execution or skipped handlers when base and subclass subscriptions are resolved together.
reproduction: Subscribe bound instance methods across an event class hierarchy, then publish a subclass event so resolve_handlers aggregates multiple subscriber lists and _dedupe_handlers processes WeakMethod-backed wrappers.
recommendation: Deduplicate handlers by a stable identity. For bound methods, use a tuple of the target instance identity and function identity, or keep a stable key on EventHandlerWrapper when it is constructed. For plain functions, the function object identity is sufficient.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests do not cover EventBus or EventHandlerStore behavior, inheritance-based handler resolution, weak bound handlers, or duplicate subscription semantics.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add EventHandlerStore/EventBus tests with bound methods subscribed on both a base event and derived event, asserting intended single execution, and with two different instances using the same method asserting neither is dropped.
